question: How do I use Order of Execution of a Step of a Recipe Agent (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: The Recipe Agent executes a step based on its Control Recipe value, checking if it's an end of phase. title: Working with the Health Monitor Service
question: How do I configure add additional processes to be monitored (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: You can add additional Processes to be monitored by the Health Monitor Service by modifying the HealthMonitorConfig.xml file located in the Health Monitor Service's installation folder (typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Common\Health Monitor). To add a process, such as Notepad.exe, add the following within the </NewDataSet> tag: `<Executables> <Executable>Notepad.exe</Executable> <CPUCoreThresholdPercent>2</CPUCoreThresholdPercent> <PrivateBytesLimit>1146880000</PrivateBytesLimit> <PrivateBytesThresholdPercent>80</PrivateBytesThresholdPercent> </Executables>`.

title: Data Logging Compression Methods
question: What are the key specifications or limits for Data Logging Compression Methods (Classic Ui)?
answer: Logging values is an event-based function, by default, a value is logged whenever it changes. When logging values, you can specify both a time and value deadband (in the Datalog agent) to reduce the number of records that you log for a value which effectively 'compresses' your log files so you are able to store more data on the same storage medium. - Using the Value deadband: Values are ONLY logged if their change in value EXCEEDS the specified deadband value.

question: How do I use Increasing Logging Periods (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?

question: What are the key specifications or limits for OEM Licensing (Classic Ui)?
answer: In Adroit certain components require a SEPARATE license BEFORE they can be used, this is known as an OEM licensed component. Note: OEM components are usually charged for although in some cases they may be free. These OEM (separately-licensed) components are no longer specified by their associated OEM codes but now included as separate textual entries in the product license, so that users can easily see exactly which components they are currently licensed for.

title: Automatic master mode assignment
question: How do I use An automatic election for master mode at a healthy standby server will occur when: (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: An automatic election for master mode occurs when a healthy master server is removed, becomes unhealthy, or when the serverMode slot of a standby server is set to master or a master server is set to standby. The Adroit system then ensures the previous master is relegated to standby, preventing multiple master servers from existing in the cluster.

title: Historical Data Catch Up of the Newly Added Standby Server
question: How do I use Historical Data Catch Up of the Newly Added Standby Server (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: Historical Data Catch Up mirrors historical data from the master server to a newly added standby server, focusing on data collected while the standby server was offline. This intelligent mirroring is performed by the SystemDataLog agent (systemDl) to synchronize system time, and is limited to catching up data between two specified date/times for performance reasons.

title: How Maximum Demand is Calculated
question: How do I use Maximum demand calculation example: (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: Maximum demand is calculated by summing the peak power consumption during a 30-minute period. In the example provided, Adroit calculates the maximum demand as ((800*5) + (200*5) + (400*10) + (800*8) + (1500*2)) / 30 = 613.33 kVA. The predicted maximum demand for each episode is also provided, and the MaxDemand status bit would be set if the configured maximum demand limit is exceeded.

title: What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it?
question: What are the key specifications or limits for maximum demand and why should you monitor it? (Classic Ui)?
answer: Maximum demand is an additional cost for most non-domestic power users. It is the method used by your electricity provider to control how much electricity you use, especially at peak times, when your usage coincides with peak domestic usage. Your maximum demand limit is the maximum amount of electricity that you are allowed to use to run your process during peak demand times, which in South Africa is measured in kVAh.

title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations
question: How do I use Complex mode and KPI calculation (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: To allow for KPIs that have one measurement divided by another measurement (other than time), such as kWh/ton- the OEE agent supports a second measurement input slot ( input2 ). For normal OEE and KPI calculations, input2 is not used and the input type is set to Unused (0), by default. In this case: KPI% = (Total for the Shift for input1/Run time)/Target KPI If the Input type 2 field (the type2 slot) is NOT set to Unused (0), then the OEE agent is said to be in complex mode.

title: Managing Subscription Queue Length
question: How do I configure Managing Subscription Queue Length (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: The Subscription Manager queue length can be adjusted to prevent overfilling. This is done by modifying registry settings within HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Workgroup\wg.ini. Specifically, you can set the 'LocalmemAsyncBufsize' and 'LocalmemHighWaterMark' DWORD values to 2000000 and 1000000 respectively.

title: Alarming Overview
question: How do I use Alarming Overview (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: While one's intention is often to keep the operators better informed by increasing the number of alarms, the result is that operators become overloaded and confused and may even start ignoring alarms! Therefore LESS alarms are MORE effective. Alarm Management is therefore an important aspect of process control as it counteracts inefficient alarming. The alarm system is a critical component for any process, which alerts your operators when components of the process are operating outside of their normal functioning.

title: Agent Subscriptions
question: What are the key specifications or limits for Agent Subscriptions (Smart Ui)?
answer: The concept of a subscription is based on the principle of "listening" for updates from a specific Agent tag (or slot). - The process of subscribing is setting up the "listener", by registering with the underlying mechanism of the relevant agent tag. - Other traditional mechanisms usually rely on explicitly reading a data point to update a value, where as subscriptions allow the change to be sent asynchronously to any "listeners". - The result is that the subscription mechanism is more responsive and less redundant so that only actual changes are sent and only when the change occurs.

question: How do I use Order of Execution of a Step of a Recipe Agent (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: The Recipe Agent executes steps in a defined order. First, it sets the ingredients based on the Control Recipe. Next, it checks if the step is an End of Phase; if not, it proceeds to the next step. If the step *is* an End of Phase, it performs verification checks, and if successful, proceeds with the phase action.

title: Specific Status Bits of the PID Agent
question: What are the specific status bits related to PV alarms?
answer: The PID Agent utilizes six status bits to indicate alarm conditions. Specifically, statusBit16 indicates low PV below its configured low alarm value, statusBit17 indicates low-low PV below its configured loLo alarm value, statusBit18 indicates high PV above its configured hi alarm value, statusBit19 indicates high-high PV above its configured hiHi alarm value, statusBit20 indicates Ehigh Error above its eHi alarm value, and statusBit21 indicates EHigh-High Error above its eHiHi alarm value. title: The Timer Agent
question: How do I use The Timer Agent (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: This agent provides a Boolean value slot as an output, which is enabled (set to TRUE) and disabled (set to FALSE) by the agent, depending upon its current mode of operation. This slot can therefore be used as an enabling or disabling or scheduling tag for other agents. Note: Although does not provide a cold-start value, it does support real-time catch-up on a standby server from a master server, which means that if the master Agent Server fails, the timing operation will seamlessly continue.

title: PID Alarm Limits
question: What are the key specifications or limits for Limitations (Smart Ui)?
answer: Note: that whenever the LL alarm is on, the L alarm must by definition already be on. Similarly, whenever the HH alarm limit is reached, the H alarm limit will already have been passed. The alarm will not be cleared until the process value goes past the limit. When the value of the PValue or Error slot of the agent reaches one or more of these configured limits, the agent will set the relevant specific status bit . The PID agent type provides alarming capabilities for both the PV (process value) and the %Error or the percentage deviation of the PV from the SP (the required set-point).

title: Agents, Slots, Tags and their relation to Values
question: How do I use Agents, Slots, Tags and their relation to Values (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: Agents are the fundamental building blocks of Adroit . They are called agents because, in addition to containing data, like simple database records, they also usually contain the ability to operate or act on their own data. For further details, see About Agents . Note: In Adroit , the data or values contained within agents are called slots.

title: Connecting the Portal Web Service to a remote Server
question: How do I configure To connect the Web service to a remote Server computer: (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: Steps: Navigate to the SmartUI Web Service installation folder, which is typically: C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI\Webservice . - Locate the "Web.config" file in this folder and open it in a text editor, such as Notepad. Its first four lines should appear as follows: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8" ?> <configuration> <appSettings> <add key="server" value="localhost" /> - Modify the "localhost", so that the value refers to either the network name of the remote Server computer or its IP address. - Save this file and close it. .

title: Data Logging Compression Methods
question: What are the key specifications or limits for Data Logging Compression Methods (Smart Ui)?
answer: Logging values is an event-based function, by default, a value is logged whenever it changes. When logging values, you can specify both a time and value deadband (in the Datalog agent) to reduce the number of records that you log for a value which effectively 'compresses' your log files so you are able to store more data on the same storage medium. - Using the Value deadband: Values are ONLY logged if their change in value EXCEEDS the specified deadband value. Hence when the value of a logged point does not exceed the previously logged value by more than the deadband, the value is not logged.

answer: To add input locales to a Windows 7 system: - Open the Start menu, select Settings , select Control Panel . - Open the Region and Language applet. - Click on the Keyboards and Languages tab. Change the keyboard (default input) language and/or install other languages as required. To add input locales to a Windows XP system: - Open the Start menu, select Settings , select Control Panel . - Open the Regional and Language Settings applet. - Click on the Languages tab. The Text Services and Input Languages dialog will be displayed - Click the Add... button to display the Add Input Language dialog.

title: Basic principles of server mode assignment strategies in Adroit
question: What are the key specifications or limits for Basic principles of server mode assignment strategies in Adroit (Smart Ui)?
answer: The state of a cluster server is recorded in the systeminfo.serverMode (0, 1, 2 = master, standby, normal respectively) and systeminfo.serverState (0, 1 = unhealthy, healthy respectively) slots for every cluster server. A new cluster server always starts up as a standby server. The serverstate slot always starts up as healthy and remains as such unless the user changes it to unhealthy (0) via a script, expression agent or a similar means.

title: Best Practices
question: How do I configure Project Directory Structure (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: The Adroit Software should be separated from the configured project(s), since this allows for easier backups, upgrades etc. For this reason, a directory for Adroit projects should be created at the root drive (or wherever the data files are required to be stored), typically called ' C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default ', this project folder should contain the following directories: - \CSV, which should contain all your exported data. - \CustomAgents, which contains all the custom agents created for the project.

question: How do I use Expressions using status slots (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?

answer: If you want the Agent Server to monitor that each connection remains healthy and to close unhealthy connections, then implement the following registry setting on the Agent Server computer: This setting enables the Agent Server to monitor the PINGs it received from each client and to also specify the required timeout value, in seconds, where if a PING has not been received within this time period then the connection to this client is deemed unhealthy and this connection (channel) is closed by the Agent Server. question: How do I use MultiState Operation (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?

answer: This file is created when an Alarm agent is exported to store its alarm routes that have been configured. The filename adheres to the following naming convention: xxxxx- ROUTLST.CSV, where xxxxx represents the name of this Alarm agent. title: Routing to Audio Devices
question: What are the key specifications or limits for Routing to Audio Devices (Smart Ui)?
answer: Routing an alarm to an audio device has the effect of incrementing or decrementing the specified slot that must be of type boolean or integer. New alarms cause the slot value to be incremented, and acknowledgment of these alarms will cause the value to be decremented. If the start slot of the Beeper agent is used, it will activate a repetitive beeping sound in the PC speaker. The sound pitch will become higher each time the start slot is incremented by a new alarm, and will be lowered when an alarm is acknowledged and the slot decremented.

title: Secondary Port Disabled
question: How do I troubleshoot Secondary Port Disabled (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: A device goes into recovery whenever a Read or Write transaction fails. This failure is a 3 step process: - Adroit requests an update from the front-end device. - Timeout Phase: the request is sent to the front end device, and times out or gives an invalid response. - Retry Phase: Step 2 is repeated for the number of retries configured.

title: Secondary Port Enabled
question: How do I troubleshoot Secondary Port Enabled (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: Adroit can make use of a secondary port to cater for the possible failure of some communications hardware component. For this to be effective, the hardware used by the secondary port should be totally separate (e.g. extra serial card and cable). A device goes into recovery whenever a Read or Write transaction fails. This involves a port switchover, and only occurs once in any transaction. The driver then runs through Steps 2 and 3 using the secondary port.

title: Time Stamping
question: How do I use Time Stamping (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: When the agent subsequently sends a subscription update to another agent, or picture element Behaviour, the same timestamp value is passed on. For example, if the Alarm agent receives a subscription update, it will route the timestamp it gets to whichever printers, event logs, alarm lists and beeper agents it has been configured with. Adroit achieves its accuracy by data at the point of creation whenever possible. Scanned values get their timestamp from the data packet returned by the front-end device, if the protocol driver is exception based and implements a time-stamping protocol.

title: What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it?
question: What are the key specifications or limits for maximum demand and why should you monitor it? (Smart Ui)?
answer: Maximum demand is an additional cost for most non-domestic power users. It is the method used by your electricity provider to control how much electricity you use, especially at peak times, when your usage coincides with peak domestic usage. Your maximum demand limit is the maximum amount of electricity that you are allowed to use to run your process during peak demand times, which in South Africa is measured in kVAh. Consequently monitoring your maximum demand can result in considerable savings and reduced power usage.

It is the method used by your electricity provider to control how much electricity you use, especially at peak times, when your usage coincides with peak domestic usage. Your maximum demand limit is the maximum amount of electricity that you are allowed to use to run your process during peak demand times, which in South Africa is measured in kVAh. Consequently monitoring your maximum demand can result in considerable savings and reduced power usage. adroit scada adroit smart other maximum demand should monitor help key specifications limits

title: Working with the Activity Monitor
question: What are the key specifications or limits for Display the Driver information on the Activity Monitor (Smart Ui)?
answer: The Driver Monitor lets you view all the devices configured on the remote Adroit Server. The options available are: - You can configure a Refresh Rate and a Filter. - The filter is a regular expression that lets you potentially filter messages to only display, for example, messages regarding specific agents. - Example Expression: Agent[2-4], Random - filters messages containing either "Random" or "Agent2", "Agent3" and "Agent4", other messages are hidden. - Additional Options include exporting the data in the window to various file types.

title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations
question: What are the key specifications or limits for Available time (Smart Ui)?
answer: Whereas KPI calculations are performed against runtime, OEE calculations are calculated against the time that the process/machine is available for production. The OEE agent therefore uses the BOOLEAN available slot (or the optional BOOLEAN tag reference availableTag ) to determine the maximum . - This slot should be ON when the machine/process is supposed to be running. - If the process/machine is under maintenance or operators are at lunch/tea, this slot should be OFF.

title: Condition Bits (not directly modifiable by the user)
question: How do I use Condition Bits (not directly modifiable by the user) (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: Because the agent bit might have been set by the user or system - and we don't want to lose this information - all agent condition bit values are derived by combining slot condition bits with the agent condition bits. For this purpose, the agent status retains a raw and a derived status word. If an agent bit is therefore set before one of its slot bit are set, it would still remain set when all slot bits are reset. Condition Bits fan-in, which means that an agent condition bit is automatically set to 1 whenever one of the corresponding slot condition bits is set to 1.

title: Control Bits (user modifiable)
question: How do I use Control Bits (user modifiable) (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: Control Bits fan-out, which means that a slot control bit becomes set or reset, whenever the corresponding agent control bit is set or reset. Note: Unlike Condition Bit fan-in, Control Bit fan-out does not use positive logic (nor negative logic, for that matter): when an agent bit is set or reset this action is performed on all its corresponding slot bits. Therefore if a slot control bit is already set when the agent control bit is reset, then this slot control bit will not be restored to its set state but will remain reset along with all the other corresponding slot bits. Global Inhibit .

title: TroubleShooting an Intermittent Communication Problem
question: How do I troubleshoot TroubleShooting Driver Communication Failure (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
answer: Determine which request is causing the communication failure. If the driver fails once and then succeeds on the retry, then the fault lies within the PLC and that this is NOT an Adroit problem. But, if the retry also fails then either Adroit has a bug or has been incorrectly configured. Follow the steps below to trouble-shoot the location of the problem: - Backup your database (WGP file) - Unscan all the tags to that PLC. - Save and restart the Agent Server. - Gradually add the scanning back in (in very small groups) waiting about 30 seconds between each.
